idea: How to save water at home
title: Three Simple Upgrades That Cut Household Water Waste
description: Saving water at home often starts with small, smart plumbing adjustments rather than massive overhauls. Installing high-efficiency aerators on kitchen and bathroom faucets can reduce faucet water flow by up to thirty percent without sacrificing noticeable pressure. Another quick win is checking your toilet tank valves; a worn flapper can silently leak hundreds of gallons every month. Keeping your household water pressure balanced around 50 to 60 PSI also prevents excess wear on pipes while conserving water across all fixtures. If you suspect an unseen leak behind walls or under floors, having a licensed plumber perform a routine pressure test can protect your home and lower your utility bills.
